# squatch-tuner

> Squatch Tuner: a software-strobe guitar and bass tuner core in header-only C++17 (no dependencies, no heap or locks in the audio path) that reads to a hundredth of a cent, with its measurement bench against YIN, MPM and a phase vocoder, a JACK host, and a browser demo (WebAssembly in an AudioWorklet). Exported from squatch-dsp; see EXPORTED.

106 tracked files; source by language (file count): C++ 40, JavaScript 17, Python 2.

Links are repository-relative paths. [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt) inlines every linked file in this order. Both files are generated by project-kit `llms/generate.py` from tracked files; do not edit them by hand - the drift gate (`generate.py check`) fails when they are stale.

## Start here

- [Squatch Tuner](README.md): A guitar and bass tuner that reads a string to a tenth of a cent.
- [Contributing to squatch-tuner](CONTRIBUTING.md): Thank you for helping.
- [Squatch Tuner: measured results](RESULTS.md): Measured on 2026-09-23 on an Apple M1 Max (clang 21, `-O3`, no fast-math) with the code in this commit.

## Optional

- [Squatch Tuner: CPU cost](results/perf.md): Object sizes (all of the memory, no heap): Tuner 128176 bytes, PolyTuner 233704 bytes, StrobeBank 116016 bytes, PartialChannel 14496 bytes.
- [Squatch Tuner: polyphonic accuracy](results/poly.md): Open strings from directinput_allsinglenotes.wav mixed with 0-40 ms spread and 0 to -6 dB levels; poly reading minus the mono reading of the same pluck alone, RMS c (p95 |diff|) [valid %]
- [Squatch Tuner: real DI accuracy, configuration variants](results/real-variants.md): Real DI: 275 notes that ring at least 1.5 s, from 2 file(s); each algorithm runs continuously over the whole file; re-pitch test +7.0 c.
- [Squatch Tuner: real DI accuracy](results/real.md): Real DI: 275 notes that ring at least 1.5 s, from 2 file(s); each algorithm runs continuously over the whole file; re-pitch test +7.0 c.
- [Squatch Tuner: synthetic accuracy](results/synth.md): Synthetic matrix: 12 notes E1..E6 x 8 trials, detune uniform ±50 c, 48 kHz input.
